title: Cooperative cis-interactions between ectodomains of TCRαβ CD3 subunits enable mechanotransduction
abstract: TCR signaling poses a mechanical problem: pMHC binding occurs at the TCR{beta} ectodomain (ECD) head, whereas ITAM phosphorylation occurs on CD3 cytoplasmic tails. Chemistry cannot bridge this >10 nm gap, so the two events must be coupled through the TCR-CD3 interface, involving conformational allostery allowing force-based regulation. Although weak ECD cis-interactions between TCR{beta} and CD3 have been proposed to contribute to this coupling, their kinetics and mechanical competence remain elusive. Here, we quantify TCR{beta}-CD3 ECD cis-interactions in a pseudo-cis configuration by two-dimensional affinity and single-bond force spectroscopy, finding that TCR{beta}-CD3{gamma}{epsilon} and TCR{beta}-CD3{delta}{epsilon} bimolecular interactions have low affinity and rapid kinetics, yet form catch bonds. Critically, concurrent engagement of CD3{gamma}{epsilon} and CD3{delta}{epsilon} generates cis-cooperativity, yielding a stronger and longer-lasting CD3{gamma}{epsilon}-TCR{beta}-CD3{delta}{epsilon} trimolecular catch bond than the sum of the two dimeric bonds, with force-stabilized lifetimes matching those of agonist TCR-pMHC trans-interaction. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal an expanded, cooperative, and asymmetric contact network, making CD3{delta}{epsilon} more force-responsive and susceptible to conformational change than CD3{gamma}{epsilon}. Interface mutations do not alter force-free affinities but remodel force-dependent cis-bond profiles, leading to an inverse correlation with trans-bond profiles and T cell signaling. These results define cooperative ECD cis-interaction as a mechanically regulatable allosteric coupling element at the TCR-CD3 junction important to antigen recognition and signal initiation.
relevance_reason: Applies molecular dynamics simulations to TCRbeta-CD3 ectodomain complexes alongside force spectroscopy, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) MD methodology, and (c) mechanistic application to mechanotransduction.

title: Importance of nonlinear long-range electron-phonon interaction for the carrier mobility of anharmonic halide perovskites
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Houtput, Ingvar Zappacosta, William Wenborn, Serghei Klimin, Samuel Poncé, Jacques Tempere, and Cesare Franchini
The carrier mobility in many materials is dominated by scattering of the carriers with phonons. It is often calculated using only linear, one-electron–one-phonon interaction. Here, the authors present a first-principles calculation of the mobility including the nonlinear, long-range electron-phonon interaction, for the representative halide perovskite CsPbI3. It is shown that the temperature dependence of the carrier mobility decreases by about 10% due to the one-electron–two-phonon interaction, which is attributed to the strong anharmonicity and low phonon frequencies present in halide perovskites.
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L200301] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026
relevance_reason: First-principles electron-phonon calculations of carrier mobility in CsPbI3 use explicit atoms and DFT, advancing nonlinear electron-phonon methodology, satisfying (a)-(c).
